items.title: Default OAuth apps for external AI agents are now generally available
items.excerpt: ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Claude Code, and Cursor can now connect to Azure Databricks MCP servers, including the Genie One MCP server, using default OAuth client IDs. An account admin doesn't need to create an OAuth app. See Default OAuth client IDs .

items.title: AI Functions Unity Catalog permissions is now generally available
items.excerpt: AI Functions Unity Catalog permissions is now generally available . Metastore admins can use Unity Catalog permissions on the system.ai schema to control which task-specific AI Functions users in your organization can run. Contact your Databricks account team to enable this feature. See AI Functions Unity Catalog permissions .

items.title: Improved Lakeflow Performance Observability will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
items.excerpt: Starting on or after November 25, 2026, Improved Lakeflow Performance Observability will be available by default for eligible workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Lakeflow Jobs now show query performance metrics and insights at the job level for supported tasks. You can view job-level data volume metrics and use the Optimize button to open Genie Code to help improve queries with performance insights. Query profiling is supported for serverless compute, SQL Warehouses and Lakeflow Pipelines. See View query performance metrics for serverless jobs .

items.title: Editing files in Unity Catalog volumes is now generally available
items.excerpt: You can now edit files in Unity Catalog volumes directly in the workspace file editor, without downloading and uploading them again. Open a file from Catalog Explorer or from the schema browser in a notebook or the SQL editor. See Edit files in a volume .

items.title: Databricks ADBC connector for Power BI and Microsoft Fabric (Generally Available)
items.excerpt: This release is part of the broader ODBC-to-ADBC transition for Power Query connectors described in the Transition from ODBC to ADBC drivers in Power BI and Microsoft Fabric documentation. What’s new Existing connections in your semantic models, dataflows, and paginated reports continue to work unchanged — the migration path is currently opt-in per connection, per workspace, or per tenant. Highlights: Improved security - ADBC drivers incorporate security enhancements, such as memory safety and garbage collection. No changes to existing behavior - This transition moves away from the embedded ODBC drivers that ship with Power BI. It does not change behavior for the ODBC connector when you use a separately installed ODBC driver. Efficient large dataset support - ADBC provides a set of standard interfaces for interacting with Arrow data, which is especially efficient at fetching large datasets with minimal overhead and no serialization or copying. Supported authentication - Databricks ADBC supports OAuth (user), OAuth (M2M / Client Credentials), and Microsoft Entra ID. items.title: QuickBooks connector is available in Beta
items.excerpt: The managed QuickBooks connector is now available in Beta in Databricks Lakeflow Connect. Use the connector to ingest accounting data such as accounts, customers, vendors, items, invoices, bills, payments, and journal entries from QuickBooks Online into Azure Databricks. The connector uses OAuth user authorization and supports incremental ingestion with delete capture.

items.title: v2.0.0-dev.41-test-pypi
items.excerpt: 2.0.0-dev.41 Released September 23, 2026 Features [Lake Compute] Read AWS Databricks Unity Catalog tables using Databricks profile PAT/OAuth M2M credentials, declaration-aware validation, and dbt debug attach parity. Existing fs catalogs.yml entries continue to use type: unity . Existing local Unity attach options in config.lakecompute must move to config.duckdb ; Lake Compute access is read-only and Unity model writes are unsupported. Fixes Fix modules.re functions silently dropping keyword arguments (flags=, maxsplit=, count=) ( #15508 ) Emit only changed columns in Databricks column-tag alter diffs ( #16246 ) Emit only changed keys in Databricks relation-tag SET TAGS diffs ( #16248 ) Implement TableRepr methods index_of_value_in_column and count_occurrences_of_value_in_column to fix Fusion panic in dbt_utils.get_query_results_as_dict() Copy config.group onto the top-level group for source and singular tests, matching dbt-core ( #15930 ) Make insert_gateway_label idempotent so gateway host resolution no-ops when the label is already present, instead of relying on a caller-side guard Set tags on operation nodes so on-run-start/on-run-end hooks are discoverable when running dbt-cor
